scope: Eight bounded no-fork substitution contracts through four shell aliases compare GNU output, status and private file effects. Normal output capture, local REPLY, nested substitutions, return, subshell exit, closed stdout, errexit and EXIT traps exercise temporary descriptor and source-string lifetime. All child logs are retained; native GNU findings remain separate

results.name: bash:normal
args: v=outer; x=${ v=inner; printf output; }; printf "%s:%s\n" "$v" "$x"

results.name: bash:return
args: x=${ printf output; return 7; printf unreachable; }; printf "%s:%s\n" "$?" "$x"

results.name: bash:nested
args: printf "%s\n" "${ printf one; printf %s "${ printf two; }"; }"

results.name: bash:errexit
args: set -e; x=${ set -e; printf hidden; false; }; printf unreachable

results.name: bash:exit-trap
args: trap 'printf exit >&2' EXIT; printf '%s\n' "${ printf hidden; exit 7; }"
